correctness.rationale: For each of 27 length-three prefixes, exact recursive extension by 0,1 or wildcard accepts precisely a four-mer whose matching set is disjoint from the previously covered set. Necessity follows because duplicate coverage cannot be undone, sufficiency because a terminal union of all 16 four-mers is then a disjoint partition; every string follows one unique path. Each extension contributes at least one new factor so depth is bounded by 16 and full length at most 19. C++17 integer-bitmask enumeration and independent Python direct-window expansion both visited 15840 nodes and agreed on all ten profile entries totaling 385. Python checked all 385 words against a separate explicit multiplicity definition and exactly 97 symmetry orbits. Sample witnesses match the original paper. No infinite-order generalization is claimed.

value.rationale: The original literature motivates the natural exact invariant: number of wildcard universal partial words at fixed alphabet and order, and explicitly calls for enumeration. Order four is the first rich binary parameter with both two- and three-wildcard nontrivial families. The complete length-vs-wildcard polynomial shows precisely which compression lengths are attainable and their multiplicities, while 32 nontrivial reversal/complement orbits and an exhaustive independent witness list give reusable construction/benchmark data. The result is a motivated full finite classification, not an arbitrary single statistic or a routine rephrasing of the known ordinary de Bruijn count.
